purpose: Thử cả ngôn ngữ đồ họa lẫn bối cảnh; ảnh concept hư cấu, không model hoặc gameplay

prompts.A: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE wide 16:9 concept of a possible PLAYABLE GAME SCREEN, not a poster. A radically GRAPHIC visual direction for an ancient-Vietnam-inspired living-world RPG. Medium is bold HAND-CARVED WOODBLOCK PRINT with flat registered ink colors, powerful black carved outlines, limited irregular hatching, broad unmarked shapes. Absolutely do NOT make photorealistic or painterly realism, no 3D lighting, no soft gradients, no tiny realistic texture everywhere. Exactly five visually distinct print inks: charcoal black, warm ivory paper, muted mineral green, iron-oxide red, pale ochre. Slight ink registration offsets and coarse carved-edge imperfections; tactile print, no calligraphy. Scene idea: a village adapting to rising floodwater. In elevated flattened 2D three-quarter perspective, a raised thatched granary on timber legs is at upper left, a connected zigzag of bamboo walkways crosses pale patterned floodwater. Central adult protagonist carrying one grain sack has paused at a fork: one path to a family at a crowded raised platform, the other to the granary where an elder and laborer organize sacks. Six well-separated villagers maximum, bold expressive adult silhouettes, readable physical work not battle. On lower right a narrow ferry and boatperson wait beside the end of walkway; the ferry is transport, not a repair workshop. Drowned fenceposts, a few large banana-leaf shapes and stylized wave lines imply river landscape. Strong playable paths between nodes, generous calm ivory water, buildings simplified into decisive flat shapes, people substantial enough to read at screen size. Composition has striking asymmetry and rhythm like an authored folk-print-inspired game, but is original fiction, NOT a claim of an actual ancient Vietnamese print tradition. No dense tiny village vista. Do not include the riverside boat repair yard or protagonist seen over shoulder from previous images. No text, letters, UI, frame, title, map legend, logos. No ornate East Asian tile pagodas, torii, Chinese lanterns, armor, glowing magic. Make the woodcut VISUAL STYLE unmistakable at a glance.
prompts.B: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE wide 16:9 mock GAME SCREEN in unmistakable crisp PIXEL ART, an entirely different graphic language from naturalistic painted river scenes. Professional authored 2D pixel RPG environment, visible deliberate square pixel clusters on one consistent low-resolution grid (approx 480x270 native appearance displayed at nearest-neighbor scale), stepped silhouettes, tightly controlled 24-color palette, selective dithering and purposeful tile shapes. No antialiasing, no blur, no smooth painted gradients, no realistic photography, no watercolor, no vector outlines, no high-detail oil painting disguised as pixel art. Scene: a busy but readable ancient-Vietnam-inspired BRONZE CRAFT WORKSHOP in the fictional Đồng Đỏ region, in elevated three-quarter / isometric cutaway perspective. A bamboo and thatch workshop with its front wall absent reveals a small clay furnace at left, one craftsperson tending a crucible with long tongs, stone-and-clay molds arranged on a low bench, cast bronze hand tools cooling nearby, stacks of charcoal and folded woven mats. At center, adult protagonist in simple indigo woven tunic speaks with an older craftsperson beside an unfinished plain bronze vessel; right outside the workshop a villager waits with a broken agricultural tool and a basket. Four or five clear individual figures, not a crowd. A walkable earth courtyard connects workshop, a tiny store shelter and a tree with broad stylized leaves. No combat or heroic weapons showcase. Palette: warm clay reds, dusty pale earth, oxidized green bronze, deep indigo cloth, pale cream daylight; small hot orange furnace is one controlled accent. Broad value groups make floor and movement route quiet, workstations and people distinct. Materials implied economically with pixel clusters, not by covering every surface in noise. Rural Vietnamese vernacular huts and clothing treated as fictional game art, not archaeology proof. Foreground and background on same sharp pixel grid, no depth-of-field. No riverboat repair scene. No UI, words, title, labels, border or logo. The entire image including characters and vegetation must look like actual pixel art, not painted concept art.
prompts.C: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE wide 16:9 imagined GAME SCREEN with a radically distinct CUT-PAPER THEATER aesthetic. All scenery and adult human characters look assembled from hand-cut dyed paper, bold irregular silhouettes, visible paper fibers at edges, solid matte colored layers, tiny tactile cast shadows ONLY between stacked paper planes. Side-on 2.5D composition with 6-8 shallow flat overlapping planes. No realistic skin, no photographic textures, no naturalistic brush painting, no pixel art, no rounded plastic toys, no actual 3D-model deliverable. Imagine an original evening community market/festival scene in a fictional ancient Vietnamese river settlement. Horizontal footpath runs across lower middle through a modest riverside gathering, beneath a single large twisting tree rendered as overlapping dark cut shapes. Adult protagonist in a red-brown vest stands near center facing an elder seated beside a folded woven cloth and simple wooden ancestral emblem. Two neighbors are trading rice bundles and pottery near a small bamboo table on left; to right a child beside parent watches reed skiffs and clay oil lamps along the landing. 5-6 clear people maximum, simplified expressive puppet silhouettes with individual poses and adult proportions; no chibi heads, no long line of identical figures. Behind them, the river is a broad calm light indigo paper band, a low reed island and sparse stilt-house silhouettes recede; an ivory paper moon partially behind one flat cloud. Palette is an intentional five-color nocturnal design: deep aubergine, dusty indigo, pale lilac-grey, warm rice-paper ivory, restrained coral-red accent. No teal-orange LUT or rainbow glow; lamps are tiny ivory holes in dark shapes, not bloom halos. Bamboo posts, woven baskets and asymmetrical cloth strips have graphic cut shapes, NOT rows of Chinese red lanterns or pagoda roofs. A sense of ordinary social life, beliefs and whispered stories, no giant visible gods or supernatural plot claim. Give this the charm of an imaginative handcrafted interactive theater, with a clear walking plane and conversation focal point, not a picturesque tourism landscape. No riverboat repair workshop. No text, letters, HUD, frame, title, logo or watermark. This is an image-only visual experiment, not a historically validated festival.
